subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Studying the genome (DNA) of organisms has improved classification because it:
options: Proves that all species are identical
Shows how closely related species are by comparing their DNA
Replaces the need for naming organisms
questions.explain: Comparing DNA reveals evolutionary relationships, leading to changes such as the three-domain classification system.

questions.q: Why do fossils provide incomplete evidence for evolution?
options: Fossils are too recent to be useful
Fossils cannot be dated at all
Many soft-bodied organisms decayed without forming fossils, leaving gaps in the record
questions.explain: Many early or soft-bodied organisms left no fossils, so the fossil record has gaps and is incomplete.

questions.q: Which is a real example of genetic engineering?
options: Dogs bred for a calm temperament
Bacteria modified to produce human insulin
questions.explain: Bacteria can be genetically modified to make human insulin, used to treat diabetes.

questions.q: The three-domain system, proposed by Carl Woese, divides life into:
questions.explain: Woese used genetic analysis to propose three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the difference between selective breeding and genetic engineering?
options: Selective breeding transfers genes; genetic engineering chooses parents
They are exactly the same process
Selective breeding chooses which organisms breed; genetic engineering transfers genes directly between organisms
Both involve changing genes with enzymes only
questions.explain: Selective breeding selects breeding pairs over generations, while genetic engineering directly moves a gene into an organism.

questions.q: Which of these could cause a species to become extinct?
options: A new predator or disease and loss of habitat
questions.explain: New predators, disease, habitat destruction or environmental change can all drive a species to extinction.

questions.q: A herd of giraffes lives where food is high in the trees. Over many generations, longer necks become common. The best explanation is that:
options: Giraffes stretched their necks and passed this on
Giraffes with longer necks survived better and reproduced, passing on the alleles
All giraffes decided to grow longer necks
The trees caused the necks to grow
questions.explain: Natural selection: giraffes with naturally longer necks reached more food, survived and passed on those alleles.

questions.q: Selective breeding for desirable traits over many generations can cause problems because reduced variation may lead to:
options: Inbreeding, making the population vulnerable to disease or genetic defects
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces the gene pool, so a single disease or defect can affect many individuals (inbreeding).

questions.q: A farmer breeds the cows that produce the most milk together over many generations. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Choosing parents with a desired trait (high milk yield) to breed together over generations is selective breeding.

questions.q: Which of these provides direct evidence for evolution?
options: Fossils showing how organisms have changed over time
questions.explain: Fossils show how species have gradually changed over millions of years, providing evidence for evolution.

questions.q: Whose work is most associated with the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.q: Which of these is a key part of natural selection?
options: Individuals with advantageous variations are more likely to survive and reproduce
All organisms in a species being identical
Organisms choosing to change to suit their environment
Characteristics changing only within one lifetime
questions.explain: In natural selection, individuals with advantageous inherited variations survive, reproduce and pass on those alleles.

questions.q: Extinction occurs when:
options: A species becomes endangered but survives
A species temporarily moves to a new area
No individuals of a species remain alive anywhere
questions.explain: Extinction is when there are no remaining individuals of a species left alive.

questions.q: Two organisms are classified in the same genus. This means they are:
questions.explain: Sharing a genus means organisms are closely related; the more groups shared, the more closely related they are.

questions.q: Genetic engineering involves:
options: Transferring a gene from one organism into another
Exposing organisms to sunlight to change genes
Breeding two organisms over many generations
questions.explain: Genetic engineering transfers genes from one organism into another, e.g. inserting a human gene into bacteria.

questions.q: How can the development of antibiotic resistance be slowed down?
options: Not finishing the full course of antibiotics
Only prescribing antibiotics when needed and finishing the full course
questions.explain: Reducing unnecessary use and always completing the course helps stop resistant bacteria surviving and spreading.

questions.q: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as MRSA are a problem because:
options: They are killed instantly by all antibiotics
They reproduce too slowly to spread
Existing antibiotics no longer kill them, so infections are hard to treat
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive treatment, making infections difficult to cure and able to spread between people.

questions.q: Selective breeding (artificial selection) involves:
options: Letting nature choose which organisms survive
Humans choosing organisms with desired traits to breed together
questions.explain: In selective breeding humans choose parents with desirable characteristics to breed over many generations.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism is named using its:
questions.explain: Binomial names use the genus (first, capitalised) and species (second), e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.q: Why did it take a long time for Darwin's theory to be widely accepted?
options: It conflicted with religious beliefs and the mechanism of inheritance was not yet known
No one was interested in biology
questions.explain: Darwin's theory challenged religious views and lacked a known mechanism of inheritance (genes were not yet understood).

questions.q: One disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Can reduce genetic variation, increasing the risk of disease
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces variation (inbreeding), making organisms more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: Carl Linnaeus classified living things into groups starting with the largest, the kingdom. Which order is correct (largest to smallest)?
options: Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
Species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
questions.explain: The Linnaean order from largest to smallest is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
